pk.context: 1 mg oral, single dose, healthy adults

tell: Its two active metabolites, 4-hydroxyalprazolam and alpha-hydroxyalprazolam, circulate at under 4% of the parent's levels.

clues.text: It is 80% bound to serum protein, mainly albumin. It is extensively metabolized, primarily by CYP3A4, and excreted mainly in urine.
A white crystalline powder with a molecular weight of 308.8 and no appreciable solubility in water at physiological pH.
Under an NDA, tablets come in 0.25, 0.5, 1 and 2 mg strengths.

The boxed warning covers opioid co-use, abuse, misuse and addiction, and dependence. Contraindicated with strong CYP3A inhibitors except ritonavir; drowsiness (41%) and dry mouth (15%) are most common.
In adults, acute treatment of generalized anxiety disorder, and treatment of panic disorder with or without agoraphobia.
It binds the benzodiazepine site of GABA-A receptors in the brain, enhancing GABA-mediated synaptic inhibition.
The generic name begins with A and has ten letters.
